THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 04.06.2019, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 CRL.M.C. NO.3818 OF 2019 2  ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
2.

The petitioner herein, a Tea Company represented by its Proprietor, is the 4th accused in C.C.
No.2564 of 2014 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Wadakanchery.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Wadakanchery
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid case, the accused are being proceeded against for having committed offence punishable under Sections 3(1) (zz) (v) & (xi), 26(1), 26(2)(i) and 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 and Rules 2.1.3.4(iii)(c) and Regulations 2.10.1.1. of the Food Safety Standards (Food Products Standards & Food Addictives) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety Standards (Food Products Standards & Food Addictives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that the 3rd accused in the aforesaid case had approached this Court and by Annexure-A4 order, the entire proceedings were quashed.

It is submitted that on 02.11.2017, Annexure-A3 order has been issued by the Food Safety Standards Authority of India calling upon the Commissioners of Food Safety of all States/Union Territories to refrain from launching prosecution for non-confirmation of limit of iron fillings in respect of cases where samples were picked up or tested prior to 19.05.2016.

entities.text: Food Safety Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
In the very same order,
the officers were advised to withdraw all prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016, either under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 or under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
In view of the above, the instant proceedings are also liable to be quashed, contends the learned counsel.

4. Heard the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. Paragraph Nos. 6 and 7 of Annexure-A4 order passed by this Court, are extracted below for easy reference.
"6.
When the matter was taken up today, the learned Additional Director General of Prosecution has filed a statement.
Along with the statement, the statement of the Food Safety Officer, Chelakkara is also produced.

In the said statement, the Food Safety Officer has stated as follows:
"As per FSSAI order dated 2 nd November 2017, it is stated that "Commissioner of food Safety, All states/Uts are, therefore, directed not to launch prosecutions for non-conformance of limit of iron fillings for cases where samples were picked up/
tested prior to 19.05.2016.
They are also advised to withdraw all such prosecution launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954."

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the sample was taken on 08.10.2013, which is much prior to the cut off date prescribed by FSSAI.

In that view of the matter, I am of the view that the petitioner is entitled to succeed."
6.
The petitioner herein is also entitled to the benefits of the above order.

The proceedings are,
therefore, liable to be quashed.
In the result, this petition is allowed.

Annexure-A1 complaint and all further proceedings pursuant thereto against the petitioner now pending as C.C. No.2564 of 2014 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Wadakanchery, are quashed.
